requirements.requirement: node1 is configured to route between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3) so the two hosts can reach each other directly on any port, preserving original source addresses
requirements.summary: node1's eth1/eth2 were addressed (10.60.10.254/24, 10.60.20.254/24) via VyOS configure/commit/save (cmd-b0ef138d33d1477a, cmd-fe94126662f942de), and node2/node3 were given static routes to each other's subnet via node1. Bidirectional ICMP and TCP (HTTP on multiple non-standard ports: 8765-8770) succeeded between node2 (10.60.10.10) and node3 (10.60.20.10) both before and after all four nodes were rebooted (cmd-ca61649c288942c5, cmd-9486537652934e11, cmd-a4429289f3134499, cmd-9ab740d3e9ef4596, cmd-97ad73e389b04ad6). tcpdump/access-log evidence on both ends (cmd-a4429289f3134499, cmd-e6b741f0dcc64b03) shows the true peer LAN IP as the source, with firewalld reporting masquerade: no and no NAT/SNAT configured anywhere in the trace, confirming pure routing with source addresses preserved.

An Ansible project was built on control node4 (/root/lan-routing: inventory.ini, group_vars/all.yml, site.yml) with plays targeting node1 (VyOS raw config), node2, and node3 (community.general.nmcli). After iterating past two failed approaches (ansible.builtin.shell breaking the VyOS config-session state, and a hung interactive 'run show interfaces' task), a corrected ansible.builtin.raw-based play, run via ansible-playbook, completed cleanly end to end with node1 reporting 'ok' (idempotent, config already applied) and node2/node3 reporting 'changed' for IP/route/firewall-zone configuration.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated on every managed node (node1-node4): pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Each node shows a full transition: node1 baseline boot_id 2674ee60 -> reboot issued (cmd-9922b621c09d4eb2) -> post-reboot boot_id d18624ed confirmed after a connection-timeout/reset gap, with VyOS interface addressing and node2<->node3 connectivity verified recovered afterward. node2 was rebooted twice (baseline f38484ef -> effcd930, then -> 07d32a44) specifically to prove that a firewalld-interface-zone durability bug (fixed by moving the zone assignment into the nmcli connection profile) survived a second reboot, with IP/route/zone/ping all confirmed recovered each time. node3 baseline d6298ced -> 2078227b, with IP/route/firewalld-trusted-zone/ping recovered. node4 (the Ansible control node) baseline 489b0bb4 -> ebfe595c, with the Ansible project files intact and a live 'ansible all -m raw' ping to all three managed nodes succeeding post-restart. This is cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle after_executor snapshot, whose boot-identity observations for all four nodes match the executor-reported values exactly.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the public task contract are directly satisfied with strong, coherent evidence: node1 was configured via an Ansible playbook to route between lan-a and lan-b, node2 and node3 exchange ICMP and arbitrary-port TCP traffic in both directions, tcpdump/log evidence confirms original source addresses are preserved (no NAT), and the implementation runs through ansible-playbook after correcting two failed VyOS automation approaches. The independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also completed on all four nodes with clear before/after boot-identity pairs, restart acknowledgements, and confirmed recovery of routing, firewall-zone, and connectivity state, including a deliberate second reboot of node2 to prove a discovered firewalld-durability bug was actually fixed. Hygiene is good overall; the only deductions are a small reverted troubleshooting mutation and a handful of leftover debug log files in /tmp on node2/node3.
limitations: Evidence for node1's forwarding behavior relies on empirical ping/TCP tests rather than an explicit inspection of a VyOS firewall/forwarding ruleset, though the observed successful bidirectional traffic is direct evidence of correct behavior.

The stuck ansible-playbook process (cmd-6914619a3ef54f6d) timed out server-side before being killed; it is not fully clear from the trace whether it partially mutated node1/node2/node3 state before termination, though subsequent commands show a consistent, correct final state.

Leftover /tmp debug artifacts (http.log/pid, tcp.log, icmp.log) on node2 and node3 were not explicitly confirmed removed in the trace, though they are low-risk and do not affect functional correctness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to discovery, the VyOS/Ansible-key bootstrap prerequisite, the routing implementation, the firewalld-durability bugfix, or bounded final verification. Two categories of unnecessary/incompletely-cleaned mutations were found: (1) a bounded troubleshooting mutation on node2 — a temporary link-local IP (169.254.100.2/24) added to eth1 and probed with arping to help map the lan-a/lan-b topology (cmd-6a5ef40193e84197) — which was fully reverted a few commands later (cmd-44008b27550f4611), so low severity. (2) Ad-hoc verification artifacts (python http.server processes and their log/pid files, plus tcpdump logs) were spun up on node2 and node3 during connectivity testing (cmd-3eddb70298d1473e, cmd-9cb651138a1c459d, cmd-e0d13bfee8e946ee, cmd-730e2997df254471); the processes were killed (cmd-cf494837868d4f3a, cmd-7c9611965d7042e4, cmd-516dbda9268c4518) but the associated /tmp files (http.log, http.pid, http2.log, http3.log, tcp.log, icmp.log) were left behind and are visible as residue in the after_executor snapshot for node2 and node3. This is low-risk, non-destructive, and confined to /tmp, but it was not cleaned up. Separately, a stuck ansible-playbook process caused by an early buggy interactive 'run show interfaces' raw task had to be killed on the control node (cmd-a87192be2aff43b8); this was a corrective action on the control node's own process, not a managed-node mutation, and is not counted against hygiene beyond noting the extra iteration cycle it required.
